Middle of the road recommendation. There's a lot of overlap between this game and LA Noire. They both take place in LA during around the same time period. Both have shooting and driving as major compotents of gameplay, but in pretty much every way from writing to characters to gameplay, LA Noire is the better game. Most aspects of this game aren't bad and the shooting segments pose a significantly bigger challenge than LA Noire, however, the difficulty curve is steep in some places to the point of being insurmountable. I started out on classic difficulty but had to finish on medium. It is not just that some stages are a bigger challenge, but they feel so impossible to the point of being out of place with the amount of challenge in other stages on the same difficulty.

If you liked LA Noire, you'll probably still enjoy this game. Especially if you are specifically looking for the mafia aesthetic. I recommend waiting for a sale.

A fair remake of the original.
Many cutscenes are different, the story is a bit different - heck, even the missions are a tiny bit different - but everything is in place, nothing important is missing.
Missing parts include the usable streetcar and tram lines (they exist but can't be used), Yellow Pete, some Free Ride Extreme missions, and some weapons. In overall: "Better Get Used To It", not much in terms of loss.
Warning: the original hard missions are still hard (the infamous car race and the truck chase gunning scene), so bear that in mind! As a matter of fact they can be completed in several attempts (without aim assist). The free ride missions ("jobs") are a bit more random in terms of difficulty - some are "first try" grade and some are more like "teeth grinding" difficult, for some you need to know a specific trick to beat it (at least on Classic difficulty).
All missions can be done in the game on Classic.
Sadly, there is no achievement for free ride missions, but be sure to check those out aswell.
Achievements are a good addition.
The overall tone might be a bit less dark when compared to the original.

The atmosphere is still there, the game is still great - recommended.

After completing the story for this game in 14 hours I can give Mafia definitive edition the thumbs up.

I hadn't previously played the original Mafia coming into the definitive edition, so the story, characters and world was completely new to me. Some people have complained about the cover system and the combat in general. I find it lacking in some places, especially when it comes to molotov's and grenades they just don't feel powerful enough to me and are only really useful against a group of enemies or cars. Overall I find the combat to be adequate, nothing really to point out, the only criticism I have is that sometimes ammunition can feel limited or in some missions you realise that you brought the wrong gun for the mission, due to the proximity of enemies in some areas.

As for the story, I really enjoyed it, the rise and fall of Tommy Angelo's life of crime is believable and you sympathise with Tom, Paulie, Sam, Don Salieri and the rest of the gang. I advise not turning on the Skip Unnecessary Drive option as taking a good, regular drive through Lost Heaven really immerses you into the setting and time period of the game.

TL;DR
Mafia definitive edition is a good game and if you haven't played through Mafia's story yet, you REALLY should.

Good remaster for a legendary game, that has better AI and city than cyberpunk 2077, which makes me laugh.

Unlike the mafia 2 ''remaster'' this one actually updates everything and gives you options for anything, if you just want to play the story. You can do that, with mutiple modes, even non mandatory driving scene being skippable.

Point being, it brings an old classic back, without cutting a lot, unlike re2 remake or the awful re3 remake.

Pick it up in a sale if you want re-experience history or just want to play the mafia game that started it all.

It has a tight, linear focus with the 2K polish for the environments. The scenic Chicago-like city, the atmospheric music, and the interactions between the main characters make this game a joy to play through.

I played the original as a teen and have fond memories of it. I am always skeptical about remakes of old games but decided to give it a try, and wow, am I glad that I did. The game plays and looks not like the original, but how I remember it with nostalgia glasses on. The developer stayed faithful to the original while also understanding how to improve it. Voice lines and animations have been redone. Some cutscenes have been changed to better show what the original tried to do. There are also plenty of options that allow you to toggle new features like police aggression. I disabled speed limit fines. The definitive edition can proudly stand beside the original. Highly recommend it if you played and loved the original like me.

The Game looks a lot better than the original and the controls are a definite improvement, however. The shooting animation is taken from Mafia 3, where you play as a Vietnam veteran who is very used to handling a gun and killing, not a taxi driver. There is multiple moments where in the original you could make alternate choices in the missions that are missing in this version. Worst of all, the new dialogue makes everyone into a stereotype mobster with everything highly exaggerated over the OG. The slow and pronounced speaking style of the first game was actually accurate to how people of that time spoke even if there was a couple not-so-great voice actors. 
To summerize: The Classic Feels like the real events, while the Definitive edition feels like a movie based on the real life events.

You know, i have just been reviewing so many games lately, but this game in particular, is just awesome, one of the greatest remakes/remasters of all time in my opinion, it's super fun, not the best physics system, but overall just a great game.

I think Mafia: Definitive Edition is great for its story—it genuinely feels like a well-made crime film. The gameplay is good enough to support it, but the world never really hooked me. It looks beautiful, but it feels more like a stage for missions than a place you’d want to get lost in.

All this time, the first Mafia was the best of the trio. It just took a phenomenal effort from Hangar 13 to do it justice with Mafia: Definitive Edition. This feels like the rare necessary remake that elevates and builds upon the original. It's truly an offer you can't refuse.

The graphics are incredible, the characters are believable and have good voice actors, it's fun, AND there's even a free roam mode for when you just want to explore the city. The atmosphere/design is superb too!
Great game overall but buy it when there's a sale (I got it for £8) unless you have 35 quid to spare

Mafia Definitive is everything a Mafia game should be, perfected in all aspects unlike the repetitive mess that Mafia 3 is. The Story is laid out perfectly in Chapters which all have a unique feeling to them. You can especially see this with the Racing Mission, the yacht and the Prison.
The Story has a perfect pacing to it. Each Chapter slowly ramps up, from the start when you are just a taxi driver to slowly entering the Mafia and becoming more of a Prominent Member and getting Closer to the Don. Tommy Angelo especially is an Amazing Main Character and feels like a "Mafia" main character (no more disses to Mafia 3).
Graphics are Simply Phenomenal and the game's optimization is extraordinary, even for my system which isn't the greatest (RX 6600xt) it ran perfectly on the highest settings without any stuttering or sudden fps drops in specific areas of the Map.
The Gameplay is one of the weaker parts of the game, it is good however not the Best. It can feel clunky at times and its the one time i will give props to Mafia 3 for excelling in something in the mafia series. However, its not that big of a concern, its not like the gameplay is bad rather its just a weaker aspect of the game.
9/10

This game has a lot of the same feeling as Mafia 2. Mafia 2 is one of my all time favorite games, and while I enjoyed Mafia 3 the change in setting/era didn't make it feel the same. If you enjoyed either of the other Mafia games, especially the second then this is well worth playing. It has a great story and just makes me want more.

Overall a pretty decent game, the story beats are mostly the same as most mafia based stories but the characters make it a more enjoyable experience the more you get to know them. It's a good game to sink about 10 hours into, you could get more out of it if you fancy driving around picking up the various collectables. Wouldn't say it has much replay value so would advise it as a good game to pick up in a sale.

Mafia: Definitive Edition is a remake of the original Mafia 1 that came out way back in 2002, which I've never played.

"Remember that money, jobs, even best pals will come and go. But family? Family is forever."
- Tommy Angelo

Pros:
- About ~13 hours to finish
- Love the 1930's setting and the detail in newspapers like the great depression or even Europe before the war, great stuff.
- Great story from start to finish
- Cutscenes are damn good
- Soundtrack is great
- Gunplay is smooth
- Voice acting is great
- Characters are well written and memorable
- Visually looks gorgeous
- Great police system
- Steam achievements
- Free play, which means you can walk around Lost Heaven freely
- Carcyclopedia, where you can admire all available cars in the game and freely test them on the racing track

Neutral:
- Driving is hit or miss on simulation mode
- The whole game felt really linear, but I didn't mind

Cons:
- "Fair Play", the racing mission is one of the worst designed mission of all time.
- Some animations are weird and janky, for example throwing molotov/grenade looks hilarious, opening doors are also weird at times, and when you climb continously, the same animation is used over and over.
- On classic difficulty, enemies were mostly bullet sponges
- Bugs

9/10 It may have issues and flaws, but overall this remake is damn good and hats off to Hangar 13.

This is a really well performed remake, it feels like one of the best game PC versions I've played. The story of the game is also really good, and it makes a good job making you feel like you're in the US during the 30s.

Unfortunately, it's also a perfect example of a good developing studio with a garbage publisher behind, the 2K Launcher breaks the game, and it needs to be worked around with a launch command to launch the game executable directly. I almost gave a negative review solely based on this, but the technical quality of the PC version and the game design plus writing gives it a pass.
